translationRepairs: Sajisi was a Uyghur, the second son of Aduduhuosi, the commander-in-chief of his state.
Sajisi was a Uyghur, the second son of Duohesi, the a-da commander-in-chief (dudu) of his state.
The name is 多和思 (Duohesi); 阿大都督 is his title, not part of the name, so the rendering "Aduduhuosi" fuses title and name.

When Wozhen died, his eldest son Zhibugan died young, the legitimate grandson Tachar was still a child, and a younger half-brother, Tuodie, grew arrogant and tried to displace the heir and rule in his own name.

When Wozhen died, his eldest son Zhibugan had already died young, the legitimate grandson Tachar was still a child, and Tachar's concubine-born elder half-brother, Tuodie, grew arrogant and tried to displace the heir and rule in his own name.
庶兄 means a concubine-born elder brother, not a younger half-brother.
He was later posthumously ennobled as Meritorious Minister for Pacifying the Borders and Extending Far Influence, with the temple name Xianghui.
He was later posthumously ennobled as Meritorious Minister for Pacifying the Borders and Extending Far Influence, with the posthumous name Xianghui.
諡 is a posthumous name (shi), not a temple name.

Posthumously he received the titles Meritorious Minister for Promoting Loyalty and Supporting the Dynasty, Grand Master of Proper Counsel, associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Superior Commander of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Liang, with the temple name Zhongyi.

Posthumously he received the titles Meritorious Minister for Promoting Loyalty and Supporting the Dynasty, Grand Master of Proper Counsel, associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Superior Commander of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Liang, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
諡 is a posthumous name (shi), not a temple name.

In his fourth year, with the south still restless, Yuehenai urged monopoly markets at Guang, Ying, and elsewhere. He reckoned an annual yield of more than 1,370,000 jin of iron, enough to cast 200,000 farm tools and exchange 40,000 shi of grain for the state—benefiting officials and commoners alike while helping subdue the south.

In the fourth year [of Zhongtong], with the south still restless, Yuehenai urged monopoly markets at Guang, Ying, and elsewhere. He reckoned an annual yield of more than 1,370,000 jin of iron, enough to cast 200,000 farm tools and exchange 40,000 shi of grain for the state—benefiting officials and commoners alike while helping subdue the south.
四年 is a regnal-era year (Zhongtong 4), not "his fourth year" of Yuehenai.

In the north he was received by Emperor Xianzong. His manner was composed and respectful, and the emperor commended him, assigning him to assist the Bozhier judicial officer with his seat at the old Yan capital.

In the north he was received by Emperor Xianzong. His manner was composed and respectful, and the emperor commended him, assigning him to assist the judicial commissioner Bozhier, with his seat at the old Yan capital.
卜只兒 is a person (the judicial commissioner Bujir/Bozhier), not an adjective for the office.

On later missions to Prince Batu's court he met Kaidu's scouts. The deputies went ahead, answered wrongly, and were killed. When Tielian came after, he said, "I am the Son of Heaven's envoy—will you treat me with violence?"

On later missions to the court of Batu's line [Prince Möngke Temür] he met Kaidu's scouts. The deputies went ahead, answered wrongly, and were killed. When Tielian came after, he said, "I am the Son of Heaven's envoy—will you treat me with violence?"
拔都王 here abbreviates 拔都蒙哥鐵木王 (Möngke Temür of Batu's line, s0072/s0085), not Batu himself, who had long been dead.
Kaidu, seeing Prince Batu's defenses already strong, grew subdued.
Kaidu, seeing that the prince of Batu's line [Möngke Temür] had already made strong preparations, grew subdued.
拔都王 refers to Möngke Temür (拔都蒙哥鐵木王), not Batu himself.

In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, on a hunt at Baoding, the day had grown late. He spoke calmly before the emperor to the people supplying the expedition: "This must not be allowed to disrupt your farming!"

In the fifth year of Zhiyuan he accompanied the emperor on a hunt at Baoding. When it had dragged on for many days, he calmly asked the people supplying the hunt, in the emperor's presence, "Isn't this interfering with your farming?"
從獵 means he accompanied the hunt and 日且久 means the hunt had lasted many days, not that the day had grown late; 得無…乎 is a concerned question.
He had five sons: Yelima, Duke of Qin and Commissioner of Chongfu;
He had five sons: Yeliya, Duke of Qin and Commissioner of Chongfu;
也里牙 transliterates as Yeliya (the Christian name Elijah); "Yelima" misreads 牙 as 馬.
Tuhulu, styled Qinchen, was the ninth son of Yalidashi and grandson of Yinna of the Kangli clan.
Tuhulu, styled Qinchen, was the ninth son of Yalidashi, a grandson of Yinna of the Kangli.
亦納之孫亞禮達石 makes Yalidashi the grandson of Yinna; Tuhulu is Yalidashi's ninth son, not Yinna's grandson.
Before long Grand Protectorate Prince Xiechegan recommended him to oversee the review of prison documents in the protectorate's judicial office.
Before long the Grand Jarghuchi of the Imperial Clan Court, Xiechegan, recommended him to oversee the review of prison documents in that court's judicial office.
大宗正 is the Imperial Clan Court (its chief judge), not a "Grand Protectorate Prince".

The ringleader, known as Envoy Qiao, lived at Jiujiang, where the prefect Yelima Dan took bribes to protect him. Envoys were sent to seize him; once the case was settled he was executed and displayed in the markets, and the bandits at once subsided.

The ringleader, known as Envoy Qiao, lived at Jiujiang, where the prefect Yela Madan took bribes to protect him. Envoys were sent to seize him; once the case was settled he was executed and displayed in the markets, and the bandits at once subsided.
曳剌馬丹 reads Yela Madan; "Yelima Dan" misreads 剌 and misdivides the name.
When the Uyghurs submitted as a state, Tangguzhi was seventeen and entered service with the Founder; he was entrusted to Emperor Ruizong, who said, "Tangguzhi can be entrusted with great affairs."
When the Uyghurs submitted as a state, Tangguzhi was seventeen and entered service with the Founder, who entrusted him to Ruizong, saying, "Tangguzhi can be entrusted with great affairs."
The subject of 因屬之睿宗，曰 is the Founder (太祖), who entrusts Tangguzhi to Ruizong and speaks; Ruizong is the recipient, not the speaker.

When Emperor Chengzong ascended the throne and honored the Grand Empress Yuan consort as Empress Dowager, Renzu was specially ordered to write the investiture document because of his skill in calligraphy.

When Emperor Chengzong ascended the throne and honored his mother, the principal consort, as Empress Dowager, Renzu was specially ordered to write the investiture document because of his skill in calligraphy.
大母元妃 means his mother the principal consort (元妃), not a "Grand Empress Yuan consort".

He immediately sent relay riders to recall him. Summoned to Sangge's chancellor's residence, Renzu was abruptly bound by a clerk and sent to supervise the work, with the deadline shortened: "Miss the deadline and you will face the law."

He immediately sent relay riders to recall him. When Renzu came before Sangge at the chancellor's residence, Sangge abruptly ordered a duty clerk to take him under guard to supervise the work, shortening the deadline: "Miss the deadline and you will face the law."
遽命直吏拘往督工 — Sangge ordered the clerk to escort him; the English obscures that Sangge issued the order and the threat.
The prefectural office had no salary lands, so Duo'erchi granted idle official fields to officials according to rank and kept the tax light.
The prefectural office had no salary lands, so Duo'erchi let out idle official land to the people, apportioning the acreage according to the officials' ranks and keeping the rent light.
以官曠地給民 means the idle land was given to the people (to farm), with acreage reckoned by official rank (視秩分畝); it was not granted to the officials themselves.

In Dade 2 he was named Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Administrator-General of Jiankang Circuit; before he could take up the post he was sent on imperial commission to Huaidong and Huaxi to hear the people's grievances and judge whether officials were fit for their posts.

In Dade 2 he was named Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Administrator-General of Jiankang Circuit; before he could take up the post he was sent on imperial commission to Huaidong and Huaixi to hear the people's grievances and judge whether officials were fit for their posts.
淮東、西 is Huaidong and Huaixi; "Huaxi" is a misspelling of Huaixi.

He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Subject Who Pushes Loyalty and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pingzhang of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, with the rank of Upper Pillar of State; the court enfeoffed him posthumously as Duke of Wei with the temple name Jingxian.

He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Subject Who Pushes Loyalty and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pingzhang of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, with the rank of Upper Pillar of State; the court enfeoffed him posthumously as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Jingxian.
諡 is a posthumous name (shi), not a temple name.
His great-grandfather A Hua had been chief of provisions to the Western Xia ruler.
His great-great-grandfather A Hua had been chief of provisions to the Western Xia ruler.
高祖 means great-great-grandfather, not great-grandfather (曾祖).
He dispatched Yueliyenu, Tiemie, and others as envoys, and more than twenty states submitted.
He dispatched Yuelayenu, Tiemie, and others as envoys, and more than twenty states submitted.
岳剌也奴 reads Yuelayenu; 剌 is la, not li.
His great-grandfather Ba Sihua had fought Naiman, Qipchaq, Rus', Hungary, and the Muslim states, often leading the van; Genghis Khan rewarded him with a tiger tally.
His great-grandfather Basibuhua had fought Naiman, Qipchaq, Rus', Hungary, and the Muslim states, often leading the van; Genghis Khan rewarded him with a tiger tally.
八思不花 is a single name (Basibuhua); "Ba Sihua" drops 不 and misdivides the name.
He distinguished himself in the war against Hala Zhang and was rewarded with male and female servants, a gold ingot, a silver urn, and other gifts.
He distinguished himself in the campaign against Qarajang and was rewarded with male and female servants, a gold ingot, a silver urn, and other gifts.
哈剌張 is Qarajang, the Dali (Yunnan) region conquered under Kublai, not a person "Hala Zhang".
He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Glorious Blessings with Silver Seal and Green Ribbon and as Grand Mentor.
He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Glorious Blessings with Silver Seal and Green Ribbon and as Minister of Education (situ).
司徒 is Minister of Education (situ), not Grand Mentor (太傅).
His father Minglitie'ermu'er served Kublai as bitchig and later as vice director of the imperial storehouse.
His father Minglitiemuer served Kublai as bitchig and later as vice director of the imperial storehouse.
明里帖木兒 reads Minglitiemuer (Ming Temür); "Minglitie'ermu'er" inserts spurious syllables.

His grandfather Xiaochou, after Taizu had conquered Western Xia and registered craftsmen of every sort, came forward as a bow-maker, was given the name Qieyannulan, and appointed commander of a hundred-household of bow-makers in a qielinkou mobile camp. He moved to Karakorum and died there.

His grandfather Xiaochou, after Taizu had conquered Western Xia and registered craftsmen of every sort, came forward as a bow-maker, was given the name Qieyanwulan, and appointed commander of a hundred-household of bow-makers in a qielinkou mobile camp. He moved to Karakorum and died there.
怯延兀蘭 romanizes as Qieyanwulan; "Qieyannulan" misreads 兀.
He rose through the ranks to commandant of trustworthy signals and darughachi of the Shaohi agricultural colony thousand-household office, then retired on account of illness.
He rose through the ranks to Commandant of Manifest Trust and darughachi of the Quebei agricultural colony thousand-household office, then retired on account of illness.
芍陂 is Quebei (Shaopi), not "Shaohi"; 昭信校尉 is a rank title.
Duoluotai's son Tuo'huan began in the night guard, worked as a translator in the Censorate, and was appointed supervising censor.
Duoluotai's son Tuohuan began in the night guard, worked as a translator in the Censorate, and was appointed supervising censor.
脫歡 is romanized Tuohuan (Toghan); the apostrophe in "Tuo'huan" wrongly splits the syllables.
In year 23 he was appointed pillars of state, Guanglu Dafu, and vice premier of the Yunnan branch secretariat for all circuits.
In year 23 he was appointed Supreme Pillar of State, Guanglu Dafu, and Pingzhang of the Yunnan branch secretariat for all circuits.
上柱國 is the singular honorific rank Supreme Pillar of State, not "pillars of state".
the third Dashiman, who rose to silver-glitter Ronglu Dafu;
the third Dashiman, who rose to Yinqing Ronglu Dafu (Grand Master of Glorious Blessings with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon);
銀青 refers to the silver seal and blue ribbon, not "silver-glitter".

In year 9 he was promoted to pillars of state, silver-glitter Ronglu Dafu, and left chancellor of the Huguang branch secretariat. Imperial gifts came month after month without fail, and the region grew calm.

In year 9 he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State, Yinqing Ronglu Dafu, and left chancellor of the Huguang branch secretariat. Imperial gifts came month after month without fail, and the region grew calm.
上柱國 is the singular rank Supreme Pillar of State; 銀青 is not "silver-glitter".
He had five sons: Yilianzhen, Tulut, Dasi, Qielie, and Antan.
He had five sons: Yilianzhen, Tulu, Dasi, Qielie, and Antan.
禿魯 is Tulu; "Tulut" adds a spurious final t and conflicts with "Tulü" in s0543.
